## About yourselfs

<br><br>

Please fill out the [Welcome Survey](https://unipadova.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2n275jqWjcN34i2) by Thursday, October 1st to help me better tailor the course contents to your background and goals. <br> It only takes 2 minutes!

## Course outline

::: {.nonincremental}

20-hour (2 CFU) Small Group Activity in blended modality, <br> with a first theroretical part online (10 hours) <br> and a second practical part in person (10 hours):

::: {style="font-size: 1.1em;"}

- `r fa("heart-pulse", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `What happens in the body?` <br>
Psychophysiology of the stress response <br>

- `r fa("microchip", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `How can we measure it?`  <br>
Introduction to wearable tech <br>

- `r fa("magnifying-glass-chart", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `What can we learn about technology users?` <br>
User studies & ambulatory monitoring <br> <br>

- `r fa("laptop-code", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `Hands on wearables and biosignals` <br>
Practical sessions

:::

:::

## Video lectures on theory, methods & applications

::: {.nonincremental}

`r fa("heart-pulse", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `What happens in the body?`

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}

  1. The Psychophysiology of Stress: From Stressful Exposures to the Autonomic Response
  2. Stress, Cognitive Appraisals and Recovery
  3. Physiological Markers of Stress and Recovery
  
:::
  
`r fa("microchip", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `How can we measure it?`

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}

  4. Wearable Technologies and Biosignals: An Introduction
  5. ECG & PPG to measure Heart Rate and Heart Rate Variability
  6. Electrodermal Activity and Skin Conductance
  7. Accelerometry & Actigraphy to measure Physical Activity and Sleep
  8. Can We Trust Wearable Sensors? Validity, Artefacts, Ethics and Privacy

:::

`r fa("magnifying-glass-chart", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `What can we learn about technology users?` 

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}

  9. Wearables for User Studies: Human–Technology and Technology-Mediated Interaction
  10. Wearables in the Wild: Ambulatory Assessment and e-Health

:::
:::

## Practical sessions on cases studies, signal recording, pre-processing, & visualization

::: {.nonincremental}

The second part includes five in-person meetings <br> with practical activities in small groups:

1. Wearable demos, cases studies, and research questions

2. Research protocols and data recording

3. Signal pre-processing in `r fa("r-project", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")`

4. From signals to user-study results in `r fa("r-project", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")`

5. User study showcase

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}

Participation to the in-person practical sessions is strongly recommended to to fulfill the requirements for the small group activity. You are free to use your own laptop or the computers available in the room (yes, we'll be in a computer room).

:::

:::

## Optional textbooks

::: {.nonincremental}
::: {style="font-size: 0.9em;"}

The course material (interactive video-lectures, slides, articles, datasets, and other educational resources) will be available in English on the course Moodle platform, covering all the main course contents.

Yet the following **OPTIONAL** textbooks are recommended for those wishing to further explore the topics covered in the course:

- Stern, Ray, & Karen (2001). *Psychophysiological Recording* (2nd edition), Oxford: Oxford University Press

- Sazonov (2021). *Wearable Sensors: Fundamentals, Implementation and Applications* (2nd edition), London: Academic Press

- Mehl & Conner (2012). *Handbook of Research Methods for Studying Daily Life*, New York: Guildford Press

:::
:::

## Evaluation and assessment criteria

::: {.nonincremental}
::: {style="font-size: 0.9em;"}

There is no final exam. The course is assessed on a pass/fail basis based on the assignments completed throughout the course and the practical group activities.

Particular attention will be posed to the **group project** developed in the practical part and presented during the very last meeting. This will consist in designing a **wearable-based research protocol applied to user research**, where students will be required to demonstrate their ability to:

- Design data acquisition protocols using wearable technologies

- Pre-process and analyze biosignals using R

- Critically interpret the obtained results

- Effectively communicate results through reports and presentations

The assessment will consider methodological and terminological correctness, quality of analysis, critical thinking, and clarity of presentation.

:::
:::
